title: Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence
text:
Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence

How do you remember the dimensions of a room you could barely see? Perhaps through the distance between footsteps, the sound of a door closing, or the way an echo travels down a corridor. For someone who has been denied the ability to see or move freely through a space, these fragments may be the only record of its architecture.

title: Exhibition Artifact / Configuración Visual
text:
Exhibition Artifact / Configuración Visual

The Exhibition Artifact (Artefacto Expositivo) arose from a commission to build a temporary support to exhibit architectural models developed by students of the UNIACC School of Architecture during a celebration of the academic community. In response to this brief, the project proposes to expand the possibilities of the exhibition display, understanding that a structure designed to hold objects can, at the same time, create an environment capable of hosting a collective gathering.

title: House Duas Marias I / Canoa Arquitetura
text:

title: Hotel Tepoztlán / Taller Carlos Marín + Pasquinel Studio
text:
Hotel Tepoztlán / Taller Carlos Marín + Pasquinel Studio

Located between Tepoztlán and Amatlán in the State of Morelos, the Hotel Tepoztlpán designed by the Carlos Marín and Pasquinel Studio Workshop Offices integrates the topography, the landscape and the views of the Tepozteco in a master plan where 4 buildings with different architectural programs explore the virtues of the site. The land was an abandoned plot, where wild vegetation, along with several medium and tall trees were located naturally on the site. From the beginning, this natural condition and respect for the flora of the site was a determining factor for positioning each of the volumes that comprise the project. Another condition that the terrain presents is its rugged topography, the access volume -a staple of pigmented concrete- is located at the foot of the sidewalk, and as we go deeper into the terrain we discover the 4 buildings, the terrain dictated the terrain and program of each of the buildings. The gentle ramps and staircases allow us to reach the pool area, which is -2.5m from the access level, while the room building makes the first forced stop for the user to the center of the land and to an altitude of - 1.20m.

title: Canal Beach Nature Resort / Atelier Bugio
text:
Canal Beach Nature Resort / Atelier Bugio

The property, located in the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentina Coast Natural Park, features three main areas: a higher ridge area, a plateau area, and an extensive valley oriented northwest, extending all the way to the sea. The intervention stems from a thorough analysis of the territory with the aim of establishing a strong relationship with it, incorporating it without altering it. It is governed by a fundamental premise: to align the experience of the surrounding natural environment with the very experience of staying in the hotel.

title: Snake Building / C+S Architects

A series of collegial workshops in Hasselt initiated the design process and assigned the plots to each office (a2o Architekten, C+S Architects, De Vylder Vynck and DRDH).

title: Room for Body and Soul: 7 Unbuilt Healthcare Facilities from the ArchDaily Community
text:
Room for Body and Soul: 7 Unbuilt Healthcare Facilities from the ArchDaily Community

Few programs carry as many meanings as healthcare. Depending on the context, health can refer to the treatment of disease, the prevention of illness, physical rehabilitation, or a broader condition of physical, mental, and social well-being. The following projects, shared by ArchDaily readers, offer a specific response to each of these understandings, from hospitals organized around diagnostic and surgical efficiency to centers where sensory regulation, contact with nature or community life sit at the core of care. Together, this group of unbuilt or unfinished projects also offers insight into concepts of health that extend beyond injury or illness toward a more holistic understanding of well-being.

title: Design Museum Gent / Carmody Groarke + ATAMA + RE-ST
text:
Design Museum Gent / Carmody Groarke + ATAMA + RE-ST

After four years of intensive renovation and expansion, Design Museum Gent will opened its doors close to UNESCO World Heritage sites. What was once a charming but fragmented ensemble of buildings is now a renewed, forward-looking museum that brings together history, innovation and sustainability. The transformation includes both the restoration of listed buildings dating from the 16th to the 20th century and the addition of a striking new wing that gives the museum a fresh, contemporary appearance.

title: Connecting Old and New Through a Ceramic Facade
text:
Connecting Old and New Through a Ceramic Facade

Refurbishing an operational industrial complex means working within an architecture shaped by daily activity and circulation. At HTBA (HealthTech Bio Actives), a manufacturer of bioactive ingredients for the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and food industries, Martín Lejarraga Oficina de Arquitectura reorganizes and upgrades the industrial facility in Beniel while respecting its production logic.

title: BIG Unveils Timber Mixed-Use Development for New Siegenthalergut District in Switzerland
text:
BIG Unveils Timber Mixed-Use Development for New Siegenthalergut District in Switzerland

BIG has been selected to design a 13,000-square-meter mixed-use development within the new Siegenthalergut urban district in Thun, Switzerland. Commissioned by Frutiger AG, the project, titled "Nachwachsende Stadt" (Growing City), brings together four timber buildings accommodating two hotels, residential units, and commercial spaces. Designed in collaboration with August + Margrith Künzel, the proposal was selected through a design competition organized by Frutiger AG in coordination with the city of Thun. The development is among the first two plots scheduled for construction within the larger Siegenthalergut district, and is expected to begin no later than 2028.

title: Skroget / Rare Collectiv
text:
Skroget / Rare Collectiv

Almost 500 kilometers above the Arctic Circle, Båtsfjord lies at the edge of Norway, shaped by the sea, the climate and a strong fishing tradition. Known as Norway's fishing capital, the town is also home to a diverse international community. With harsh weather often limiting opportunities to gather outdoors, the municipality envisioned a new public place by the harbor. Their request was a sauna complex with meeting spaces to encourage people to connect and to enhance the sense of community.

title: Mexican Studio COLECTIVO C733 Named First Recipient of the Siza Award for Public Architecture
text:
Mexican Studio COLECTIVO C733 Named First Recipient of the Siza Award for Public Architecture

Mexico-based COLECTIVO C733 was named the inaugural recipient of the Siza Award for public architecture, established by the Serralves Foundation. The first edition marks the 10th anniversary of the Serralves Foundation's Álvaro Siza Archive and aims to recognize architectural generosity and public-space engagement, in honor of the Portuguese architect's vision. Like Siza's body of work, the award is open to the international community. COLECTIVO C733's public infrastructure portfolio includes markets, cultural facilities, transport hubs and public landscapes across Mexico, such as Bacalar Eco-Park, Guadalupe Market, Tapachula Station, Nacajuca's Music House community center and Matamoros Market, as well as their work with Mexico's Ministry of Agrarian, Territorial and Urban Development (SEDATU) in vulnerable regions and along the U.S.–Mexico border.

title: What Happened to Parametricism? How a Style Blurred Into a Look
text:
What Happened to Parametricism? How a Style Blurred Into a Look

In September 2008, at a series of sessions organized alongside the 11th Venice Architecture Biennale under the name of the Dark Side Club, a text was presented that announced, for the first time since Modernism, a new style for architecture. Parametricism as Style, written by Patrik Schumacher, then a partner at Zaha Hadid Architects, called it "the great new style after modernism" and recast Postmodernism and Deconstructivism as "transitional episodes" that had prepared its arrival. What the manifesto proposed was a design logic in which every element of a project, from the urban plan down to the tectonic detail, the interior and the product, would be treated as a variable, so that form could differentiate continuously and adapt to the shifting demands placed upon it.

title: Student Dining Block at S. R. University / SJK Architects
text:
Student Dining Block at S. R. University / SJK Architects

The design of the Student Dining Block at S. R. University creates a visually light, scaled-down structure with humble proportions that deliberately belies the scale of its operations—the facility provides over 16,000 meals to 5,400 students every single day. Wide landscaped streets, amphitheatre-style stairs, and courtyards are integrated into the design, elevating the dining area into a lively communal hub that nurtures conversations and camaraderie.
